title: Rose
description: A pairwise puncture-capped rose factorization follows by recursively applying the PC daisy relation. The framed inner-boundary rose remains to be developed.

sections.Surface and conventions: A disk with marked points treated as punctures; twists enclosing a single point are trivial.
sections.Derivation: Apply the recursive PC daisy relation until every factor encloses a pair of points. The four-point version also follows by applying the PC lantern to the first three-point daisy factor.
sections.Braid factorization: Every pair twist has an explicit conjugated braid word; exact Artin-action checks cover three through six points.
sections.Planar mapping class diagrams: The four-point six-factor continuation is available in the boundary-twist playground.
sections.Standard mapping classes: All factors are positive pairwise Dehn twists, with under-going support curves where required.
sections.Equivalences and transformations: The playground applies the PC daisy and PC lantern as separate, checked substitutions.
sections.References: See the linked derivation and Margalit–McCammond, Geometric presentations for the pure braid group, Section 4.
